title: A better annual rain forecast gave no clear extra wet-deposition skill at 128 US sites in 2005-2024
abstract: We tested whether improved annual rain forecasts add wet-deposition skill on a published NADP panel of 128 US sites and nine ions. Models used coefficients fitted through 2004 and past-only levels for 2005-2024. A frozen autoregression reduced weighted log-rain mean squared error by 17.2% against a fixed historical mean, with a 95% crossed bootstrap range of 9.0% to 25.8%. Yet its added deposition gain was -0.03 percentage points, with limits of -1.93 to 2.60. The fixed-mean control was added after the first results and is exploratory. An exact shared-error bound showed that the observed-rain gain of 25.3% could tolerate weighted RMS log-rain error of 0.293 with zero residual cross moment, but only 0.111 for all shared-error alignments. At equal rain error of 0.20, constructed response gains ranged from -25.6% to +52.6%. These constructions use response outcomes and are sensitivity tests, not forecasts. Weather error alignment, not accuracy alone, controls forecast value in this model. The panel overlaps prior work. Revised data, a short record, selected sites, a shared rain input in the target and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and audit instructions are supplied.
